## Terms

### compound index

- **compound index** · self — **Compound indexes** are indexes that contain references to multiple fields. Compound indexes improve performance for queries on exactly the fields in the index or fields in the [index prefix.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-compound-index-pr · aka: compound indexes, compound-index, composite index, multi-field index, index-compound — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound/create-compound-index.md

### ESR rule

- **ESR rule** · part · aka: ESR, Equality, Sort, Range, equality-sort-range, equality sort range, ESR guideline, Equality Sort Range rule, equality-sort-range-rule

### index prefix

- **index prefix** · part — Index prefixes are the beginning subsets of indexed fields. Compound indexes support queries on all fields included in the index prefix. · aka: index prefixes, prefix of the index, prefix subset, leftmost prefix, key prefix — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#index-prefixes

### covered query

- **covered query** · part — To determine whether a query is a covered query, use the db.collection.explain() or the explain() method. See Covered Queries. · aka: covered queries, covered, covering index, covering indexes, index-only, PROJECTION_COVERED, index covers, totalDocsExamined: 0 — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/

### index selectivity

- **index selectivity** · measure · aka: selectivity, selective index, cardinality, high cardinality, low cardinality, distinct values, sort order of the index

### index intersection

- **index intersection** · part — Index intersection does not help a sort that needs an index separate from the query predicate; indexed sorts require a compound index whose key order matches the filter and sort. · aka: index intersections, AND_SORTED, AND_HASH, intersect indexes, intersection of indexes — https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v6.0/core/index-intersection/

### multikey index

- **multikey index** · hyponym — Multikey indexes can cover queries over non-array fields only if the index tracks which fields cause it to be multikey. They cannot cover queries over array fields. In one forum case an index including an array field forced a FETCH and examined about 5.1M documents; the same index without that field · aka: multikey indexes, multikey, multi-key index, multikey index bounds, multikey-index-bounds, isMultiKey, multikeyPaths, parallel arrays, indexed array, array field index — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/

### $elemMatch

- **$elemMatch** · related — The document with `_id` equal to `3` is the only document that matched the [`$elemMatch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemmatch.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-elemMatch) criteria. · aka: elemMatch, compound bounds, intersecting bounds, compounding bounds, bounds intersection — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemMatch.md#elemmatch-https-www-mongodb-com-docs-manual-reference-operator-projection-elemmatch-md-mongodb-projection-proj-elemmatch-with-multiple-fields

### partial index

- **partial index** · hyponym — Partial indexes with an $or filter are a known planner weak spot: forum reports (MongoDB 6.0.4 and 6.0.13) show a query repeating the identical $or still got COLLSCAN or another index, while a query with plain conditions (e.g. comments:{$exists:true}) used it. No accepted fix is shown on the threads · aka: partial indexes, partialFilterExpression, partial filter expression, partial-index — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/partial-index-not-covering-or-query-filter/220425

### sparse index

- **sparse index** · hyponym — - Sparse indexes include or exclude documents *solely* based on the presence of the indexed field (or multiple fields, for sparse compound indexes). · aka: sparse indexes, sparse: true, sparse, index-sparse — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#comparison-with-sparse-indexes

### sort direction

- **sort direction** · part · aka: index key direction, reverse sort, in-memory sort, blocking sort, sort without index, sort order of the index, prefix of the index supports the sort

### index anti-pattern

- **index anti-pattern** · problem · aka: anti-pattern, anti-patterns, antipattern, unnecessary indexes, too many indexes, redundant index, redundant indexes, duplicate index, index bloat, low selectivity, unused index

### index key

- **index key** · part — Index keys from the same array compound their bounds only if (a) the keys share the same path up to but excluding the field names, and (b) the query uses $elemMatch on that path. If the query predicates cover several array fields without $elemMatch, MongoDB compounds the leading scalar field with on · aka: index keys, key pattern, keyPattern, index entry, index entries, indexed field, indexed fields — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/multikey-index-bounds.md

### single-field index

- **single-field index** · contrast — A single-field index whose key is the leading prefix of a compound index (e.g. {field:1} next to {field:1, other:1}) is redundant: the compound index serves the same filter. Keep the compound index and drop the prefix one. The manual's example drops {time:1} as covered by {day:1, time:1}, though tha · aka: single field index, single-field indexes, single field indexes — https://mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/design-antipatterns/unnecessary-indexes/

### query planner

- **query planner** · related · aka: explain, winningPlan, IXSCAN, indexBounds, index bounds, FETCH, COLLSCAN

### index

- **index** · hypernym — Index `{ item: 1, price: 1 }` is a [partial index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#std-label-index-type-partial) and only indexes documents with `price` field greater than or equal to `Decimal128("10")`. · aka: indexes, indices, indexing — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/planCacheStats.md#mongodb-shell
